title: THE STRONGEST SORCERER VS. THE KING OF VILTRUMITES — Satoru Gojo vs. Grand Regent Thragg

sequences.title: The Encounter
sequences.objective: Establish atmosphere, character and tension; plant the lit city, the trace-cursed-energy read, and Gojo's perch.
sequences.logic: Geography first: the aerial plants west = lit city + sunset (screen-left) and east = dark towers (screen-right) before any character appears. Thragg's arrival is an announcement (heavy, not massive, tier). His survey ends on the lights, which are his leverage (T1-19), and the cut reveals Gojo standing literally in that line. Mutual assessment in two halves: Thragg classifies an obstacle (S1-05). Gojo's Six Eyes plant R1, a civilian-level trace on an absurdly dense body, and R5, location without intent (S1-06); he peeks with one bare eye and drops the blindfold back, arrogance that Seq 3 cashes in (S1-07). Two lines; Gojo's lazy step onto the arm puts him further in the way and lands him on the boundary position. Silence intercut on both. Thragg ends the talk the way he ends everything: without warning (S1-10). Infinity is deliberately never visualised in Seq 1, so Seq 2 introduces it cold. Beat timings sit within the +/-1.5 s slack to give the dialogue its 9-frames-per-word room.
sequences.music_cue: Low string drone on D, distant restrained choir, wind; solitary taiko on the landing (S1-02 f16); near-silence for the exchange (drop_out S1-08 f0); FULL silence for the final beat before the launch (S1-09 f58 through S1-10); the sonic crack breaks it.

sequences.title: The First Impact
sequences.objective: Demonstrate Thragg's terrifying physical power and introduce Infinity as deceleration, not a wall; Thragg stops attacking and starts investigating.
sequences.logic: Thragg's opening move is to end the fight with one blow (S2-01). It slows without end 1 cm from Gojo's blindfold, and grit thrown at bullet speed hangs in the gap. This is the plant Seq 7 pays off. From then on every attack is an experiment that rules out one hypothesis. Target and trajectory: a hook to the temple, a knee to the ribs, a low kick to the knee (S2-04 to S2-06). Footing: the sweep shears the mast arm, and Gojo keeps standing on nothing (S2-06, S2-07). Reflex: a feint gets no reaction, and the real strike comes from the blind flank, then from directly above (S2-08, S2-09). Thragg's eyes go from confusion to analysis: he isn't defending, something is (S2-10). Mass: a four-tonne slab stalls and then simply drops (S2-11). Speed and attention: a 300 m loop through the storm deck, then a maximum-speed dive from high behind Gojo's right (S2-12, S2-13). Gojo turns calmly to face him before he arrives. The stall is identical, and the boom wrecks the street around him but not his collar (S2-14). Thragg's conclusion is that this is a property of the space around the man, so conventional force is not enough. He withdraws to 30 m and studies Gojo with growing hostility (S2-15), which hands off to Seq 3's Blue. Gojo never defends, never moves a hand to block, and never evades: Infinity is automatic (G1-09, X1-03). His only actions are acting beats: a head tilt, a weight shift, a pinch gesture and the turn. Screen direction stays Gojo-left/Thragg-right throughout. The one reversal (S2-13) is set up by the visible contrail loop in S2-12 and restored by Thragg's backward withdrawal in S2-15.
sequences.music_cue: Seq 1's silence was broken by the launch crack. S2-01 to S2-03 are near-silent: sub rumble plus the hanging infinity_stop ring, with the score ducked under the line. The 96 BPM low percussion and electronic pulse RETURN on Thragg's reset at S2-04 f0 (one beat = 15 frames). Low brass stabs fall BETWEEN blows, never on a stall, and the music thins under every infinity_stop so the ring reads. There is a low brass hit as the mast arm falls (S2-06). Thragg's motif (descending minor third) is a STINGER on the analytical narrowing of his eyes (S2-10). It SWELLS with the climb (S2-12) and DROPS OUT 4 frames before the dive arrives (S2-13), so the boom and the ring play alone through S2-14. It RETURNS low in S2-15, with Thragg's motif over a bare pulse, handing off to Seq 3's 112 BPM.

sequences.title: The Sorcerer Takes Control
sequences.objective: Gojo's combat intelligence, Limitless, Blue, hand-to-hand and Red; contact is one-way; Thragg commits.
sequences.logic: Seq 2 ended with Thragg concluding that force alone is not enough. Seq 3 is Gojo's answer: for the first time he acts instead of waiting. Every exchange answers a question and sets up the next one. E1 (S3-01 to S3-03): can convergence pin a flyer? A Blue beside Thragg, not on him, turns the street into a debris storm. Thragg's efficient answer is a tangential burn, which holds him in place but leaves him blind behind a wall of debris. He learns the man can MOVE him; Gojo learns to use the blindness rather than the pull. E2 (S3-04 to S3-07): a second, tiny Blue self-pull through the wall puts Gojo unseen at Thragg's back. A palm with Blue at impact and a rising elbow land cleanly and barely matter: the hardest body Gojo has ever hit. Thragg's counter-grab produces the sequence's key image (S3-06): Gojo's hand holds Thragg's wrist while Thragg's other hand hangs 3 cm from Gojo's throat. Contact is one-way and chosen. Gojo uses Thragg's own thrust as the lever for a wrist throw, drives the Blue point down after him and releases it, burying him. Gojo lands between the heap and the lit city. E3 (S3-08 to S3-10): Thragg erupts unhurt, and every dangerous fragment hangs short of Gojo. A Six Eyes POV that rhymes with S1-06 shows the problem: the faint haze gives location but no intent, so Gojo reads the zero-wind-up hook late and dodges on Toji-trained instinct although Infinity would have held. Thragg's eyes catch the dodge. E4 (S3-11, S3-12): out of the pivot, a point-blank Red throws him east, away from the city, through three facades; his uniform is torn and his cape shredded. The wide shot shows the straight path, the slumped floors and the dust. Aftermath (S3-13 to S3-15): Thragg rises, wipes his split lip, smiles faintly: "Now we're fighting." He stops testing. Gojo stops clowning: the blindfold comes down to his neck, his hair falls loose, and he looks east with uncovered eyes, ready for a body that leaks no intent. Screen direction holds: Gojo left, Thragg right. Gojo's attacks travel left to right and Thragg's right to left. The only crossing is Gojo's straight self-pull into Thragg's airspace, and Gojo's descent west restores it. Real time throughout; no slow motion.
sequences.music_cue: 112 BPM (one beat is about 12.9 frames). Gojo's rising-fifth brass motif enters as a stinger at S3-01 f26 over a glassy synth arpeggio, swelling with the Blue (S3-02 f0). Brass stabs fall between Gojo's blows. The music thins to the arpeggio under the infinity_stop ring (S3-06). The groove drops out to a lone low pulse while the heap is still (S3-08 f24) and through the Six Eyes POV. A full-orchestra HIT lands on the Red release (S3-11 f6), and its tail rings over the collapse. Low brass plays Thragg's descending minor third as he rises. A HELD single low chord with the rhythm stopped (drop_out at S3-14 f30) sits under "Now we're fighting". Gojo's rising fifth swells in the strings as the blindfold comes down (S3-15 f28), handing off to Seq 4's 140 BPM taiko.

sequences.title: Viltrumite Fury
sequences.objective: Thragg's extended physical showcase AND investigation; door one (Infinity off as bait); Gojo's smile fades.
sequences.logic: Each exchange follows from the last. E1 (S4-01..03): Thragg abandons straight lines for verticals, flanks and feints, grabs instead of punches, and never stays in reach; Gojo blocks nothing, sways off the one hook he reads late, and counters with two short Blues that Thragg beats by watching the hand (he learns: move when the hand moves; Gojo learns: he won't stay still for a point-blank Red). E2 (S4-04): the slow-hand test proves the barrier judges what he is, not his speed. E3 (S4-05..08): so Thragg attacks the one thing that changed (the uncovered eyes) with dust; the fist from the murk still hangs, but Gojo must spend his big Blue to see again, and Thragg punches through its rubble. E4 (S4-09..10): the full-force roof strike tests shockwave transmission; the wave parts round Gojo and the city takes it, tearing the cloud deck (the cause of Seq 7's light shafts). E5 (S4-11..12): Gojo, unable to fix a hit-and-run fighter in the open, pulls himself into the unfinished tower; Thragg follows through its flank, and the fighters swap sides on screen. E6 (S4-13..16): door one: Gojo switches Infinity off as bait (Hanami precedent G2-11); Thragg commits and stays, breaks the collarbone and drives the spear-hand; Infinity returns at high output (X1-14), pries the grip open and stalls the spear-hand; a point-blank Red cracks two ribs and burns his chest (R6 dose), guts three floors and throws both into open sky. Sky (S4-17..18): Thragg stabilises first and watches RCT knit the bone: 'So. It is a choice.' He now knows the barrier can be off and that damage must be total. End (S4-19..20): Gojo's smile fades; Thragg attacks again. Technique count: two short counter-Blues (E1) and one self-pull (E5) per the beat sheet, plus the ledger's one large dust-clearing Blue; Infinity off about 0.4 s then raised output; Red x1 point-blank; RCT x1.
sequences.music_cue: 140 BPM taiko/toms, driving ostinato, both motifs in counterpoint from the launch (S4-01); thinned under the slow-hand test and the dust stall; peak at the tower crash (S4-12); bare under the bait; hit on the Red; ducked under Thragg's line; music drops out for the smile-fades close-up (S4-19); a stinger on Thragg's launch hands into Seq 5.

sequences.title: Hollow Purple
sequences.objective: First major cinematic peak: Hollow Purple with full identity (two separate techniques, a visible charge, fusion, a clean trajectory, a wall of imaginary mass). The lit city constrains Gojo's line; Thragg evades the core through raw speed and counters, but pays with his left forearm, his left flank and his left ear.
sequences.logic: Seq 4 ended with Gojo EAST of Thragg: the point-blank Red threw both of them into open sky. Seq 5 therefore opens with the screen direction reversed, and Thragg is charging east. His renewed attack goes for the head, the lesson of 'So. It is a choice': damage must be total (S5-01). The Six Eyes tell Gojo where Thragg is, not what he intends (R5). Gojo refuses to let Infinity answer the question Thragg is asking and leaves the plane on a Blue self-pull. The pause belongs to Thragg. He drifts, unhurried, until the lit city across the river sits exactly behind him in Gojo's eyeline (S5-02; T1-19 hostage logic). The rack focus is Gojo's read: any flat shot that misses goes into those windows. So Gojo spends almost three seconds flying up and over Thragg to the west (S5-03). That puts him back between Thragg and the lights, as in Seq 1, and restores the film's screen direction (Gojo left, Thragg right). His line now slopes down into the empty eastern district. Thragg does not chase. He banks breath and a fact: he protects the lights (S5-04), the leverage Thragg uses in Seq 6. Then the score falls away and Purple is built in three readable stages: two separate techniques with opposite behaviour (S5-05, S5-06); their effect on the world, a local darkening, bent light and trembling debris (S5-07); and the cost, in Gojo's still face and reddening eyes (S5-08). Purple takes time to charge (G1-29), and Thragg sees it: for the first time the man has needed TIME (S5-09). He launches straight down the firing line. That line is the fastest and also the most predictable, so Gojo completes the fusion and releases on it at once (S5-10). The breath Thragg banked during the relocation is what lets him throw the last-instant corkscrew. The core misses; the outer shell takes his trailing left forearm at mid-forearm, and the displacement wake flays his left flank and tears off his left ear (R7: a CREATIVE margin, with no claim about the core against Viltrumite flesh). Still spinning, he drives a counter into Gojo's ribs. It stalls in Infinity until the wake rips him away (S5-11). Purple carries on along a line chosen to cost nothing: four empty towers and a street, while everything west of Gojo stays untouched (S5-12). The aftermath sets up the next two sequences. Thragg is maimed for good, because nothing regrows (T1-47). He is no longer amused and resolves never to give Gojo time again (S5-13), which becomes Seq 6's assault. Gojo's biggest technique has missed; anything he aims, this body can dodge, so his next finish must be one Thragg cannot slip. With his eyes bloodshot, he presses two fingers to his temple and refreshes his brain with RCT (S5-14), planting the mechanic Seq 7 depends on. Neither fighter is untouched. Everything plays in real time; there is no slow motion (that is reserved for Seq 7).
sequences.music_cue: S5-01: the Seq 4 toms snap back for one bar under the renewed charge (RETURN f0) and are cut dead on the miss. S5-02 to S5-04: a suspended low string pedal on D with no percussion; Thragg's descending minor third and Gojo's rising fifth are exchanged softly. S5-05 f4: DROP_OUT, a total drop to a low sub rumble as Gojo raises his hands. Layers enter through the charge: a restrained choir (SWELL S5-06 f20), then low brass (SWELL S5-07 f6), then a high string tremolo (S5-08). Thragg's minor-third STINGER lands on his recognition (S5-09 f8) and the cluster crescendos through his anticipation. The full orchestra crests with a HIT on the release frame (S5-10 f4) and sustains under the stall, ducked so the infinity_stop ring reads (S5-11 f5), then decays under the destruction (S5-12). Sustained strings carry the aftermath (S5-13, S5-14) and thin out toward Seq 6.

sequences.title: The Domain
sequences.objective: Unlimited Void as the supernatural climax - mechanism shown, not a magic button; the touch exemption nearly saves Thragg; Gojo's gamble begins.
sequences.logic: Thragg's last leverage is the lit city (T1-19). He climbs into Purple's dust plume to deny Gojo the body-read he has relied on since Seq 3 (S6-01). The Six Eyes still find the civilian-level haze (R1): it tells Gojo WHERE Thragg is, never what he intends (R5). It coils, then snaps down and west (S6-02). The geometry gives the WHY: extended, Thragg's line runs straight down the avenue at the lights (S6-03). Seq 5 taught Gojo that anything he aims, this body can dodge; a chase loses; Purple needs time. The one thing Thragg cannot dodge is a sure-hit. So Gojo spends his single teleport (R11) to stand in the path at the west corner (S6-03 to S6-04). Thragg, true to his Seq 2-4 lessons, does not run into the stall or stop in reach: he brakes dead on the air 8 m out to re-read a man who appeared from nowhere. The plant costs him a second, because the torn ear makes his flight wobble (S6-04). In that second Gojo forms the one-hand sign in total silence and makes the call (S6-05). Thragg's Seq 5 lesson ('when he needs time, strike') makes him lunge, and the barrier closes on the first frame of the lunge, so its momentum dies with his mind (S6-05/06). The barrier registers his faint haze (R1), so the sure-hit lands. Inside, about 2.0 s of real time plays as about 20 s of perception time (logged deviation; G2-16); it is never slow motion. His flight dies with his mind and he sinks (S6-07), and his perception drowns (S6-08). One Blue pins and turns him, opening the Purple-flayed flank (S6-09). Gojo knows touch exempts (G1-32), so his three positioning touches last one frame each (one-frame pupil strobes), but a heart thrust cannot. For its duration Thragg is lucid, and his body corkscrews the heart off the line: ribs and the left lung go, the heart does not (S6-10, T1-34). His grab stalls in Infinity; Gojo pulls out, and the flood slams back (S6-11). Gojo cannot read Thragg's vitals, and every touch inside wakes him, while 2 s of flood (ten times Shibuya's dose, double Shoko's Sukuna figure) should leave him frozen afterwards. So he decides to finish by hand outside and withdraws to his corner (S6-12). The exterior cutaway runs on the objective clock: everything inside was a silent black dome for exactly 2.0 s, which makes the pre-set visible (S6-13). The void peels away with both men hanging in the air, Gojo's technique about to burn out (S6-14 into Seq 7). Gojo's lesson, that a precise blow can be slipped, is why Seq 7's finish is a Red inside the chest and not a hand for the heart. Screen direction: Gojo is screen-left and Thragg screen-right in every shot. Reverse-angle cameras face north-east or north-west, never south. Slow motion is never used.
sequences.music_cue: Seq 5's aftermath strings thin to one high line, with a tempo-less sub pulse under the climb (S6-01, S6-02). Thragg's descending minor-third motif SWELLS in fast low brass on the break (S6-03 f4) and peaks on the teleport. SILENCE (score and ambience) falls at S6-04 f20 as the hand rises; the call is delivered over total silence (S6-05). domain_open's snap (S6-06 f0) is followed by 7 frames of absolute zero, then high crystalline clusters SWELL over a sub drone and the granular information-tick bed (S6-06 f8). There is no rhythm anywhere inside the domain; a heartbeat sits under Thragg's close-ups (S6-07, S6-08, S6-10, S6-12). The bed is the flood made audible: each one-frame touch hiccups it, it DROPS OUT for the spear-hand's contact while Thragg is exempt (S6-10 f23), and it RETURNS at full on the frame contact ends (S6-11 f28). The exterior is a hard cut to SILENCE, wind only (S6-13 f0). Back inside, the clusters bend downward into the reversed shatter (domain_close) and DROP OUT on S6-14 f60, so Seq 7 opens on isolated piano-like tones over the dust.

sequences.title: The Final Exchange
sequences.objective: The most memorable 30 s: burnout, Gojo's gamble, Thragg's will, the race between Thragg's fist and Gojo's repair; one slow motion; decisive impact into silence.
sequences.logic: Seq 6 ends with the domain's two pre-set seconds spent and both men in mid-air at the west corner. S7-01 to S7-03 are a master angle and two overlapping angles of the same real second (map: screen 0-4 s = real 0-1 s). Burnout is shown by the absence of Limitless (R9): Gojo, who has floated all film, falls and skids, and there is no refraction ripple anywhere. Thragg's flight fails too, because the flood is still in him. Both are visibly spent. Gojo is bloodshot, torn at the shoulder and breathing hard. Thragg is one-armed, his flank flayed, his ear torn and his lung ruptured; he bleeds from the nose, ears and tear ducts and his pupils are unequal. That is the R8 after-effect: CREATIVE, will rather than recovery, and nothing resets. S7-04 is the decision ('Shibuya mode'). His hand rises to his temple for the repair, the Seq 5 gesture, and stops: the repair compounds the brain damage that ended Shinjuku, and the target looks frozen. He gambles on a physical finish (G1-33, G2-40). S7-05 and S7-06 (real 1-5 s, near real time): Gojo walks in while Thragg's struggle plays out (clawing, head jerks, doubled vision converging); this is his will. The Six Eyes tell Gojo where Thragg is, not when he will move (R5), so the lunge in S7-07 comes unannounced. The domain lag throws it a hand's breadth off and it craters the asphalt. The shard it throws (S7-08) cuts Gojo's cheek, paying off the Seq 2 plant in which the same shards hung. Thragg reads the evidence correctly: the man walked instead of floating, and he bleeds, so the barrier is off (S7-09). Gojo, knowing what Thragg saw, starts the roughly one-second repair, and his nose bleeds. From here it is a race. Thragg goes for the head, because Seq 4 taught him that a healer must be destroyed whole. Gojo's reinforced parry knocks the blow wide (S7-10), but Thragg takes the arm (S7-11, the Oliver precedent). Gojo cannot heal it while repairing (ch 226 trade-off, G1-38) and chooses the repair. The tear costs Thragg the fraction of a second the repair needed. Thragg's final straight (S7-12, S7-13) is total commitment: no guard, and the Purple wound turned toward Gojo's free hand. THE slow motion runs S7-13 to S7-15 (real 6.0-6.4 s). The repair completes and the nosebleed spurts. Infinity resumes on its own, near fragments stop while far ones keep drifting, and the fist stops 1 cm from the eye in the S2-02 composition. Two fingers slide into the open flank. In S7-16, Red detonates inside the chest, aimed down and east, away from the lit city behind Gojo. There is no skin barrier, and the heart is destroyed (R6; T1-34 #141). The mix cuts to silence on the impact frame. In S7-17 the shockwave crosses the intersection in silence: the backwash parts around Gojo, and the ground heave kicks the mast out of its footing and over into the crater onto Thragg. S7-18 holds the wide silhouette. Counterfactual: remove the Purple flank wound, the domain lag, Gojo's choice to save the repair or the forearm parry, and Thragg's fist lands on a burned-out skull. Strike variety: a low ground-skimming lunge, a rising straight, a twisting tear and a full-body straight, each with its own angle and lens. Screen direction: Gojo is screen-left facing right throughout; Thragg is screen-right attacking right to left. The only moves along the axis away from that are Gojo's motivated stagger west and Thragg's blast-back east. Positions: Gojo x=-7 (y=3) to x=-6.6 (skid), then x=-3.5 (walk), then x=-6 (stagger to the mast). Thragg x=+1 (y=2, then on his knee), then x=-2.6 (lunge), then x=-5.0 (final drive), then x=-2 (thrown into the crater).
sequences.music_cue: Out of Seq 6's reversed shatter, MUSIC RETURNS (S7-01 f8) as isolated piano-like tones, one every second or so, over the dust, with no pulse. It carries through the burnout, the decision and the walk (S7-01 to S7-05), with a low string harmonic entering under the walk. It SWELLS from S7-06 f30 as a low pulse fades in under Thragg's coil, accelerating. A HIT on the lunge's contact frame (S7-07 f12) drops in the 150 BPM ostinato, with both motifs colliding: Thragg's descending minor third against Gojo's rising fifth. The ostinato thins under the two reactions in S7-09 and peaks through the parry and the tear (S7-10, S7-11), with no brass on the tear. It DROPS OUT 2 frames before the slow motion (S7-12 f22). The slow motion stretches ONE chord (an event SWELL at S7-13 f0) across S7-13 to S7-15, with no rhythm. Under it, slowed heartbeat and breath, the soft repair chord, and Infinity's stalled swell and glassy ring at the stall (S7-15 f12). There is a HARD CUT TO SILENCE on the Red impact frame (S7-16 f3); only the final_impact transient lands. SILENCE holds through the silent shockwave (S7-17, no SFX at all) and the wide silhouette (S7-18), where the only sound is a faint high ring: Infinity's ring tail, at very low gain.

sequences.title: The Verdict
sequences.objective: Reveal the winner decisively, in the order the audience needs it: who is down, whether he is finished, what winning cost the man still standing, and who he is again now it is over. End on an image of Gojo's personality, set between the fallen conqueror and the city he protected, and cut to black at exactly 04:00:00.
sequences.logic: Seq 7 ends in silence on a wide silhouette through the dust. Seq 8 resolves that silhouette in four real-time shots and keeps the film's grammar throughout: the camera faces north (north-west for the push-in, the S5-14 set-up), west is screen-left, Gojo is screen-left and Thragg screen-right. (1) The verdict on Thragg comes first, from straight above (S8-01). A plan view with north at the top of frame keeps west at screen-left and shows the whole result in one image: the radial starburst left by the internal Red; the toppled traffic-light mast, Gojo's Seq 1 perch, where Thragg said 'You stand in my way', now lying over him; and Gojo at the west rim, still literally between Thragg and the lights. A warm shaft through the torn cloud deck (Seq 4's tear, still the motivated light source) lays Gojo's long, faint shadow across the crater to Thragg's boots. (2) The defeat is then made unmistakable at the body's own level (S8-02): one agonal rise of the destroyed chest, then a stillness held for 18 frames. The eyes stay open, and a fleck of ash lands on his cheek without a blink. The cause is canon-legible and planted in Seq 7: the heart is destroyed, the one injury Viltrumite healing cannot survive (#141; X1-55, T1-34), and nothing Thragg lost could ever have grown back (T1-47). There is no last word and no glow leaving the eyes; the body simply stops. (3) The survivor's cost and character arrive in one slow push-in as the score returns (S8-03). His actions follow the mechanics in order. First, only now, with the technique repaired and nothing left to fight, can his RCT go to his body (he could not repair and heal at once; G1-38), so the stump seals; his output is low after the domain and the repair, so regrowth only begins (G1-41). Second, the nosebleed, the price of the repair, stops, and he wipes it to a dried trace (nosebleed healed, nosebleed_trace stays). Third, he covers the Six Eyes again, because it rests them (G2-38) and he no longer needs them bare; the hair springs back into the silhouette from Seq 1. The cut on his cheek, the bloodshot eyes and the torn shoulder stay. 'Told you.' is said to the crater, quiet and tired: a callback to 'You should've picked an easier planet' with the cost on him. (4) The final image (S8-04) turns his back on the body and his face to what he protected. In a low, locked-off wide he stands at the left third against the last band of sunset and the lit, untouched city on the left horizon, his one hand in his pocket and his weight on one leg: the Seq 1 stance with one sleeve empty. The toppled mast and Thragg's smoke thread are to his right, and beyond them the ruined east. That is the film's argument in one composition: Gojo's losses regrow, Thragg's never do, and the lights behind Gojo were never touched. There is no slow motion; Seq 7 held the film's only slow motion. Silence carries over from Seq 7 until the cut to the survivor, and the score's last note is cut by the end of the film. No title, no tail, no black frames inside the runtime.
sequences.music_cue: S8-01 and S8-02: SILENCE carried over from Seq 7's impact (event silence at f0 of each), with no score; only Seq 7's faint high ring decaying to nothing by S8-01 f30, plus wind, settling grit and Thragg's last breath. S8-03 f0: RETURN on the cut to the survivor. Solo low brass states Gojo's rising fifth (D up to A) once and leaves it open, with strings entering softly underneath and no percussion; the score ducks about 8 dB under 'Told you.' (f68-86). S8-04 f14: a restrained SWELL in the strings as the final pose settles, and the rising fifth resolves home to D. The last note is cut, not faded, on the film's final frame (04:00:00).

shots.prompt_core: Worm's-eye shot from the asphalt, crosswalk stripes leading to the centre of an empty intersection, dark storefronts beyond. Thragg drops vertically into frame feet first, arms close to his body, his crimson cape streaming upward like a flame, and lands dead centre. The asphalt caves into a shallow crater, radial cracks race outward, a ring of grey dust hugs the ground and rolls toward the lens, and the storefront windows behind burst outward one after another in glittering sheets. Brief camera shake. As the dust thins he is revealed in a deep, compact crouch, head bowed, hands loose, no fist on the ground. The cape drifts down and settles over his back. Absolute stillness.

tactical.read: Nothing moves: the district is evacuated and dark.
tactical.outcome: Crater, radial cracks and burst storefront glass; nothing in the district answers.
tactical.learned: The people have gone. What matters lies elsewhere, and his survey will find it to the west.

shots.prompt_core: Worm's-eye view from cracked asphalt looking up at a tall white-haired man in a black high-collared uniform standing on empty air three metres above a ruined dusk avenue, blindfold at his neck, loose white hair. A massive man in a torn white-and-crimson bodysuit, shredded crimson cape rags streaming, has come up from below him: his open left hand hangs frozen three centimetres under the standing man's jaw, short of the throat, a sheet of gravel suspended in the air beneath the chin. The white-haired man looks down at him without moving. Behind them a lamp post bends toward a small white-blue point of attraction ringed by darkened space. tactical.learned: Gojo: he is reading my hands, and he won't stay still long enough for a point-blank Red. Thragg: break off whenever the hand moves; and again, he dodged.

Screen-right, a massive man in a torn white-and-crimson bodysuit with a split lip and shredded crimson cape rags floats in close at walking pace, right arm extended, palm open, reaching for the high collar; his fingers have stopped four centimetres short and hang there, a faint heat-haze refraction around the fingertips, nothing else between them. shots.prompt_core: Low-angle medium-wide shot on a mid-rise office rooftop fifty metres above a dusty district at stormy dusk. Screen-left, a tall white-haired man in a black high-collared uniform, blindfold at his neck, stands on the west parapet, hands loose, utterly still. Eight metres to screen-right a massive man in a torn white-and-crimson bodysuit has driven a whole-body haymaker into the roof deck: the slab caves into a crater, cracks race across the roof, and a dome of compressed air bursts outward behind a flash. Where the blast reaches the standing man it parts: gravel and roof fragments hang in a curved sheet a hand's breadth from his body and stream past on either side; his collar and loose hair do not stir. Warm rim light from screen-left.

tactical.intent: Thragg: force at scale. Will the shockwave itself reach him if the fist cannot?
tactical.read: Gojo watches the wave come and fold around him without moving.
tactical.outcome: The pressure front is held at the boundary; the roof, and the city, take it.
tactical.learned: Thragg: even air at that force is held.

shots.animation_notes: Massive tier. The haymaker has the sequence's longest anticipation (9 frames) because it is the biggest blow so far; hip rotation leads. The wave is drawn as a lensing dome with debris riding it; around Gojo the debris sheet bends like water round a stone. Gojo is a held cel through the wave: no cloth or hair secondary motion at all.

shots.prompt_core: Extreme wide shot from far away of a dark abandoned city skyline at stormy dusk. A visible ring of compressed air races outward from a rooftop impact across the roofs; behind it windows burst block by block in a glittering spreading wave, rooftop water tanks tumble off their steel legs, antenna masts fold flat. A column of compressed air punches up into the low storm-cloud deck and tears it open in a ragged, churning hole, and the first shafts of warm orange evening light fall through onto the district. Screen-right, an unfinished skyscraper of bare floor slabs with a yellow crane on top. Far screen-left, beyond a river, a lit city glows untouched under the sunset. A tiny dark figure stands unmoved on the struck rooftop.

tactical.outcome: Held at Gojo; the city takes it: windows blown for blocks, water towers gone, the storm deck torn open.
tactical.learned: Thragg: force alone, even through the air, will never reach him.

shots.prompt_core: Medium close-up of a tall white-haired man in a black high-collared uniform, blindfold hanging at his neck, standing on a rooftop parapet under the first shafts of warm evening light breaking through torn storm clouds. His bright-blue eyes have moved past a massive man in a torn white-and-crimson bodysuit, soft in the mid-ground and climbing out of a smoking roof crater, to an unfinished skyscraper on the skyline to the east: bare concrete floors and a half-hung glass skin. His right hand flicks two fingers toward the tower; far away, a tiny white-blue point ringed by darkened space glows inside one of its floors, and the gravel at his feet begins to slide toward it.

tactical.outcome: Gojo pulls himself toward the unfinished tower, over Thragg's head.
tactical.learned: Thragg: he is leading me somewhere. Follow anyway.

shots.animation_notes: The decision is a look, not a gesture: eyes move from Thragg to the tower and back to Thragg in 8 frames. The self-pull is G1-19 movement Blue: the body leaves on a smear frame, no run-up.

He goes through the flank: the glass curtain wall bursts outward in sheets, a steel column folds round his shoulder. f14-40: the camera runs alongside as he ploughs east down the length of the floor: concrete beams snap with spits of dust, rebar whips loose, steel columns buckle outward one after another, glass panes explode out of their frames in a racing line along the tower face, glittering in the light shafts. f40-60: the destruction front nears the far end of the floor. f60-71: the camera pushes in through a burst bay into the bare grey interior.

shots.prompt_core: Wide lateral tracking shot at dusk, level with the twenty-ninth floor of an unfinished skyscraper: bare concrete slabs every four metres, steel columns, rebar, a half-installed glass curtain wall, shafts of warm evening light falling through a torn cloud deck. A massive man in a torn white-and-crimson bodysuit ploughs horizontally through the length of one floor from screen-left to screen-right, leaving a racing line of destruction: glass panes exploding outward in glittering sheets, steel columns buckling and folding outward, concrete beams snapping with spits of dust, rebar whipping loose. Ahead of the destruction, at the far end of the floor, a tall white-haired figure in black waits inside. Shredded tarps flutter from an open bay where he entered.

tactical.intent: Thragg: follow by the straightest line, through anything in the way.
tactical.read: Gojo hears him coming through the floor and turns to meet him.
tactical.outcome: Thragg arrives inside; the floor's west half is wrecked, and now there is nowhere to slide sideways.
tactical.learned: Gojo: he comes straight. The room is ready.

shots.animation_notes: The one extravagant camera move of the sequence; keep it smooth and lateral, no roll. The destruction is structural and directional (west to east), never a fireball: beams snap, columns buckle outward in sequence, glass bursts outward. Thragg stays a readable white-and-crimson shape inside the debris at all times.

shots.prompt_core: Wide shot inside a bare unfinished skyscraper floor at dusk: grey concrete slab, steel columns, rebar, flapping tarps, warm light shafts slanting through open bays at the back. Screen-left, a massive man in a torn white-and-crimson bodysuit with shredded crimson cape rags and a split lip has just skidded to a halt, boots carving grooves in the slab, shoulders squared, facing screen-right. Eight metres away screen-right, a tall white-haired man in a black high-collared uniform, blindfold at his neck, stands with his hands loose at his sides. Concrete chips falling from the cracked ceiling drop freely around his shoulders; one bounces off his sleeve. The big man's cold eyes follow the falling chip. Dust motes hang in the light.

tactical.intent: Gojo: he never stays in reach, so give him a reason to. Switch Infinity off as bait (the Hanami precedent) and let him commit.
tactical.read: Thragg sees the shimmer vanish and the chip touch the sleeve: the barrier is down.
tactical.outcome: Thragg reads the opening he has waited for all fight.
tactical.learned: Thragg: something touched him.

shots.animation_notes: The cue must read with the sound off: hanging chips with a ripple (Infinity on) versus the same chips falling and one bouncing off cloth (Infinity off). No other change on Gojo: no aura, no pose shift beyond the out-breath. Thragg is a held cel except the eyes, which follow the chip. Infinity off lasts about 0.4 s of story time before S4-15's re-raise.

shots.prompt_core: Low medium two-shot in profile inside a bare concrete skyscraper floor at dusk. Screen-left, a massive man in a torn white-and-crimson bodysuit has crossed the floor in one surge: his right hand clamps the left shoulder of a tall white-haired man in a black high-collared uniform, the thumb driven down into the collarbone, the shoulder visibly dropped, the dark jacket tearing open there with blood blooming through. The white-haired man's face shows pain for the first time: teeth set, bright-blue eyes wide, loose hair flung forward. The big man's left hand is drawn back at his hip, fingers straight and locked together in a spear-hand, aimed at the heart. Warm light shafts and concrete dust behind.

tactical.intent: Thragg: the opening he has waited for. Pin him with the grip, then the heart (his signature finisher).
tactical.read: Gojo lets the grip land; the pain is real.
tactical.outcome: Collarbone broken; jacket torn and bloodstained; the spear-hand is in flight at his heart.
tactical.learned: Thragg: he can be held, and he can be hurt.

shots.animation_notes: The first blow to land on Gojo in the film, and it must hurt to watch: the grip deforms the jacket and shoulder; the bone break is a 2-frame drop of the shoulder line. Gojo's pain face is held for 8 frames on 1s. Thragg's grip uses the Oliver-arm precedent's economy: no flourish.

shots.prompt_core: Tight close-up on the chest and left shoulder of a tall white-haired man in a black high-collared uniform, the jacket torn and bloodstained at the shoulder. A massive crimson-gloved spear-hand, fingers locked straight, hangs three centimetres from his heart, trembling, the attacker's forearm bunched. Space around the white-haired man visibly swells: the background bends like thick glass and grit on the floor skids outward in a ring. The attacker's other hand is being pried off the bloody shoulder finger by finger, the fingers forced open and hanging four centimetres off the fabric, tendons straining. Between the two arms, the white-haired man's right hand rests two fingers on the attacker's white-and-crimson chest emblem, a tight jittering crimson point glowing at the fingertips.

tactical.intent: Gojo: fix Thragg at zero distance, with both his hands committed inside the re-raised Infinity, and deliver a point-blank Red.
tactical.read: Thragg's eyes drop to the two fingers; he knows the hand cue now, but both his arms are caught in the swelling space and he cannot break off in time.
tactical.outcome: The grip is pried open, the spear-hand stalls 3 cm from the heart, and Red is charging against his sternum.
tactical.learned: Gojo: the bait worked, and it cost a bone.

The spear-hand stall uses the standard Zeno curve; this is the blocked beat Seq 7 will mirror at the eye. Red charge per VFX bible: a tight crimson point jittering 2-6 frames (6 here).

tactical.learned: Thragg: Gojo won't let him test the barrier on Thragg's terms, and chasing in open sky gets nothing. Gojo: close range is now Thragg's game; get distance and build something.

tactical.learned: Gojo: anything I aim, this body can dodge (Seq 6: he goes for the heart by hand). Thragg: the shell alone can take a limb; never be on its line again.

shots.action: Real time. f0-12: Thragg in profile on the crater floor, head screen-right. His square jaw is still set; his black mustache is greyed with dust. Dried blood tears sit at the corners of his open, unequal eyes, froth and blood at his lips, and blood runs down his neck from the torn left ear. At frame-centre is the charred cavity of his chest, with smoke curling up out of it. Nothing moves but the smoke. f12-26: one last rise of the chest, slow and laboured, a wet rattle drawn through froth; the edge of the cavity lifts and a bubble swells at the corner of his mouth. f26-34: the chest falls, faster. A small puff of smoke escapes the wound, the bubble breaks, and the jaw slackens a few millimetres. f34-52: stillness. The open eyes stay on the torn sky above him and do not blink. At f44 a fleck of ash settles on his cheek below the left eye, and nothing answers it. The smoke thins to a thread. The Grand Regent is dead: the heart is destroyed, and Viltrumite healing cannot repair it.
shots.animatic_caption: One last breath lifts Thragg's ruined chest. Then stillness; his open eyes never blink again.
shots.prompt_core: Ground-level close-up on the floor of a crater: a fallen giant lies on his back in profile, head to the right. His square, severe face is pale and still; close-cropped black hair and a thick black mustache are greyed with dust; dried blood tears mark the corners of his open dark eyes, froth and blood sit at his lips, and his left ear is torn away. His chest, in the remains of a white-and-crimson uniform, is a dark, charred, smoking cavity. The chest rises once, slowly, a last laboured breath; a small puff of smoke escapes and the jaw slackens. Then complete stillness: the eyes stay open on the torn storm sky, and a fleck of ash settles on his cheek without a blink. Above, out of focus, lies the bent arm of a toppled traffic-light mast.
shots.animation_notes: Thragg on 2s for the breath; the smoke on 1s. The rise is slow and laboured (14 frames) and the fall quicker (8). The jaw slackens a few millimetres on the fall. No eye movement, no blink, no expression change: this is not acting, it is the body stopping. After f34 nothing on the body moves at all, and the ash fleck at f44 lands with no reaction. Keep the wound restrained: a dark, charred cavity with no anatomical detail. Continuity check: the torn left ear, the flayed left flank (camera side, at the bottom edge) and the frothy mouth are all on the camera side.

shots.action: Real time; the score returns on f0. A constant slow push-in throughout, from waist up to head and shoulders. f0-4: Gojo stands in the ruin, facing east, his head bowed toward the crater. Behind him, low on the left horizon across the river, the warm windows of the lit city burn, untouched. f4-20: with the technique repaired and nothing left to fight, his RCT finally goes to his body. He lifts what is left of his left arm a few centimetres and glances at it as a soft warm-white shimmer passes over the raw stump at the elbow for 16 frames; pale new tissue seals it, with a first faint swell of regrowth beneath. It is slow, because his output is low. f20-34: blood is still running from his nose, the price of the repair. It stops. He draws the back of his right wrist once under his nose (f24-30) and lowers it, leaving a dried smear. f34-56: one-handed, he hooks his thumb under the blindfold hanging at his collar (f36-40) and draws it up over the bridge of his nose and his bloodshot eyes (f40-50); it seats at f50. His loose white hair springs up into its tall, spiky silhouette (f50-56). The fresh cut on his left cheekbone sits just below the edge of the cloth. f56-68: a faint, tired smile at one corner of his mouth. f68-86: GOJO (quiet, to the crater): "Told you." f86-96: he breathes out; the smile stays; he holds.
shots.animatic_caption: Push-in. RCT seals the stump; he wipes his nose, pulls the blindfold up, a tired smile. "Told you."
shots.prompt_core: Slow push-in from medium shot to medium close-up on a tall, lean man with loose snow-white hair standing amid ruins at dusk, front three-quarter, looking down and to the right. His black high-collared uniform is torn and bloodstained at the left shoulder; his left arm ends at the elbow, where a faint warm-white shimmer seals the stump with pale new tissue. A fresh cut crosses his left cheekbone; blood runs from his nose, and he wipes it with the back of his right wrist, leaving a dried smear. One-handed, he draws a black blindfold up from his neck over his eyes, and his white hair springs into a tall spiky silhouette. A faint, tired smile; two quiet words. Behind him, low on the left horizon across a river, glow the warm windows of a lit, untouched city.

tactical.intent: Gojo: with the technique repaired and nothing left to fight, spend RCT on his own body at last (he could not repair and heal at once), and cover the Six Eyes to rest them.
tactical.read: Thragg is dead: no breath, no movement, the heart destroyed. There is no further threat and no need for bare eyes.
tactical.outcome: The stump seals and regrowth only begins, because his output is low. The nosebleed stops, leaving a dried trace. The cheek cut, the bloodshot eyes and the torn shoulder stay.
tactical.learned: Gojo: the gamble came within a centimetre of his skull and cost him an arm, which will come back; Thragg's losses never will.

shots.animation_notes: Gojo on 2s; every gesture is economical and a little slow from exhaustion. The RCT follows the VFX bible: a soft warm-white shimmer for 16 frames, the tissue knitting from the inside out, then pale new skin over the stump and the first millimetres of regrowth; no green, no sparkles. The wipe is one pass with the back of the wrist. The blindfold: the thumb hooks the cloth at the collar and draws it up over the bridge of the nose, and it seats at f50. The hair goes from loose fringe to the tall spiky silhouette over 6 frames with a 2-frame overshoot, as overlapping action, not a pop. The smile is one corner of the mouth, tired, not smug. 'Told you.' is barely voiced and the lips hardly move. The push never eases out; it just stops with the shot.

He ends facing west toward the lit city, three-quarter to camera, with his left side nearest the lens: the sleeve ending at the sealed stump. f10-18: his remaining hand slides into his trouser pocket. f14-20: his weight settles onto one leg and his head tilts a few degrees: the Seq 1 stance. f20-47: the final image holds. To the right the toppled mast lies across the crater, and from behind its near rim, where Thragg lies hidden, a thin thread of smoke rises and bends in the wind. shots.prompt_core: Final image: a locked-off, low-angle wide shot from street level at dusk. In the left third, a tall, lean figure with a black blindfold and tall spiky white hair stands at the edge of a fresh crater, a dark silhouette against the last band of sunset glowing low on the left horizon over a lit city across a river. He turns from the crater toward the distant lights, slides his one remaining hand into his trouser pocket and settles his weight on one leg, head tilted slightly; his left sleeve ends at the elbow. A warm rim outlines his hair and shoulders. To the right, a toppled traffic-light mast lies across the crater, and a thin thread of smoke rises from below its rim. Beyond: ruined towers, a torn storm deck, dust motes falling slowly through shafts of light.
shots.animation_notes: Gojo on 2s. The turn is unhurried: hips lead, shoulders follow, head last; the right foot pivots and the left steps (f8). The hand finds the pocket cleanly, the weight shift drops one hip, and the head tilts about 6 degrees. From f20 everything on him holds except the wind in his hair and jacket hem; only the smoke thread and the falling dust motes animate. The empty left sleeve hangs at the elbow on the camera side and must read in silhouette. The last frame is a fully composed image, not a blur, fade or dip: the film ends on it.
